verdict.rationale: Kick has first-party Rules that override AI categorization and run automatically whenever a matching transaction syncs. That is a documented event-triggered rule mechanism, and AI-native users can create these rules through the MCP connectors (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor). The scope is narrow, though: the only documented trigger is a transaction sync and the actions are about how transactions are handled. missing for 10: event types beyond transaction sync, action types beyond transaction categorization/handling, detailed rule-condition documentation, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Once a rule is created, it runs automatically every time a matching transaction syncs.
Rules let you tell Kick exactly how to handle specific transactions - overriding AI categorization with your own logic.
Query transactions, generate reports, create automation rules, and execute bookkeeping changes
